text: Done, uncommitted in the working tree on top of bc7a418. POST /v1/datasets/{d}/grants accepts an optional Idempotency-Key. The grant ID then derives from caller, dataset and key (the existing minted helper), and Catalog.grant and grantShare take that ID. A named grant keeps the time of its first issuance, so a retry presents the identical record and putGrant returns it without a second commit; the policy lock is taken first, so concurrent retries wait and see the first. Criteria: 1 same key and intent, in any action order, returns one grant and one issuance, including eight concurrent submissions; 2 the key refuses another recipient, release, action set, expiry or grant shape with 409, and different keys or no key issue independent grants revoked independently; 3 a replay after revocation is 409 and renews nothing, and a replay after the issuer lost authority is the usual 404 with nothing disclosed; 4 the console sends one key per submission, reuses it for an unchanged form after a failure and takes a new key after a success or a changed form. Requests without the header behave as before. Evidence: one law in CatalogLifecycleSuite on both catalogs; GrantRetrySuite (6 PostgreSQL HTTP tests, 4 of which fail when the key is ignored); console check grant-retry-same-key; scripts/check-postgres.sh passed (684 unit, 384 integration, crash and restore); scripts/check-console.sh passed; scripts/check-console-backend.sh passed 13 scenarios including a grant and a revocation through the real browser. Documented in docs/http-api.md and docs/http-api.openapi.json. Note for SHARE1: on D-open a steward keeps ManageAccess through her project role after handing over stewardship; only an ExplicitOnly dataset loses it.
